cost: Prompt O(rule+example+story+brief bytes); partition O(n+k*boundaries); splice O(output+fix bytes); remote calls dominate unknown latency. At most 2 calls v1, 3 v2, up to 2 per part v3 absent resume; retries after failures can repeat effects.
description: Prompts concatenate versioned rules/examples and numbered story slices; continuation includes preceding text/world brief. parts chooses k=ceil(n/max), nearest later paragraph boundary to ideal cut; splice replaces each valid 1-based @N line in order and counts writes. call rejects done before I/O/teacher; v2 rejects >2 parts then allows one repair total; v3 prefers fixed then raw, estimates before missing raw call and repair, writes fixed without revalidation.

inverse: Spliced output admits arbitrary overwritten originals and duplicate replacement histories; count is not number of changed rows. Cached fixed output admits differing original raw/repair histories. Prompt strings retain selected sentence text but do not reconstruct entire world history.
limitations: Pure parts/splice/prompt/estimate and done guard tempfile checks. No teacher invocation, DB/license query, live repair or finite-budget assurance.
